decisions.quote: If, as in Vichi et al (2009) and Lopes (2010), the study considers only if successive gains reached the criterion for contingency change, then we can state that the data here obtained replicated the ones from Vichi et al. and disagree with the ones from Lopes, since all groups reached these criteria. In this sense, the contingencies here manipulated established control over collective behaviors, being an experimental analogous to metacontingencies.
decisions.reason: Under the original study's criterion for contingency control (reaching the successive-gains criterion for contingency change), the authors explicitly state that all three groups replicated Vichi et al. (2009) and established control over collective behaviors. While the authors also conduct an additional binomial statistical test showing significance in both contingencies only for G1 and only under Contingency B for G2 and G3, they explicitly state in the Discussion (lines 642-644) that because Vichi et al. (2009) did not conduct that statistical treatment, the comparison cannot be made, and they do not argue that the original method is invalid as a test of the hypothesis.

scope_review.parent_objection: The first reply codes mixed from within-study significance differences between Contingencies A/B. Discussion says the original studies did not conduct that statistical treatment, so the comparison cannot be made. On the original criterion, all groups replicate Vichi. Resolve whether Rule 1 overall/focal successful, mixed, or methodological-flaw special verdict is supported. Do not substitute our own p-value assessment or comparison of a new statistical analysis for the original test. Read entire Discussion including critique and originals comparison. Retain genuinely unresolved if needed.

prior_reply.quote: The visual inspections which supported these analyses are not fully confirmed statistically. Considering that only two possible dividing responses were permitted (equal or unequal), the verification of contingency control over these responses depends on the confirmation that the correct responses proportion was above 50%. In G1, the total proportion of correct divisions after each winning round was 63.4% (Z=2.43; p=0.008). This higher proportion was confirmed in both contingencies (Contingency A: 60.4%, Z=2.07 p=0.019; Contingency B: 67.7%, Z= 2.89 p=0.002). In G2 and G3 the proportion of “+” signs subsequent to winnings was 58.0% and 55.1% respectively, but they were not statistically superior to 50% considering α=0.05 (G2: Z=1.44, p=0.074; G3: Z=0.91, p=0.182). Controlling relations of earnings over division responses were confirmed for both G2 and G3 under contingency B (G2: Z=2.42, p=0.007 and G3: Z=2.92, p=0.002). However, statistical significance was not reached when they were under contingency A.
prior_reply.reason: Although all groups reached the contingency-change criterion as in Vichi et al. (2009), the authors qualify that visual inspection was not fully confirmed statistically: controlling relations were statistically significant across both contingencies in only one group (G1), whereas in the other two groups (G2 and G3) control was confirmed only under Contingency B and not Contingency A.
